A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiDAR compression framework and contain readable main text and nine-page supplements. Equations, tables, figures and supplementary content can be matched reliably across the versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original KITTI and Ford compression experiments, runtime measurements, component ablations and supplementary quantitative and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original compression experiments, runtime measurements, ablations and supplementary analyses. These remain original empirical results despite being unchanged from v1.

M1.justification: GRED, shallow/deep XFP propagation, cross-entropy training and integer-only inference are retained. The notation edits in Eqs. (13)-(14) do not establish a different algorithm or implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use KITTI and Ford for the same geometry-compression task and retain the same precision ranges, sequence-level evaluations and cross-device scenarios. No dataset, domain or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain G-PCC octree, OctAttention, Light EHEM, Unicorn and RENO. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the supplementary parameter, complexity, sequence-level and qualitative comparisons. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, quantization conventions, 11-16-bit evaluations, distortion and BD metrics, training settings and timing hardware remain unchanged. Correcting the Fig. 2(a) caption does not change the metric already shown on its axis.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the GRED/XFP ablations, threshold-level sensitivity analysis, complexity measurements, sequence-wise comparisons, reconstruction examples and cross-platform demonstration. Removed pointers to supplementary material do not remove the analyses themselves.

E5.justification: Dataset-level averaging and statistical reporting practices remain unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-seed results, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Corresponding main and supplementary tables, plotted results and reconstruction examples are unchanged. For example, KITTI D1 BD-PSNR gains over RENO remain 1.887 dB for the floating-point model and 1.728 dB for the integer model in Tables 1 and 2.

T1.justification: The loss, probability factorization and mathematical treatment of quantization remain unchanged. Eq. (13) makes the weight transpose explicit, and Eq. (14) supplies previously implicit clipping bounds; these clarify notation for existing operations without changing assumptions, derivations or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: addressing HRCS with GRED/XFP and enabling deterministic cross-platform coding through integer-only inference while maintaining competitive compression and real-time speed.

C2.justification: Section 2 removes the specific explanation that GRASP-Net handles sparse geometry through PointNet-based analysis but incurs substantial complexity from its heterogeneous design. Interpretations of the proposed method's results, Ford's limited training data and the supplementary parameter-efficiency limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The supplement retains the same architecture details, coordinate and occupancy operations, quantization instructions, optimizer settings, training duration and hardware. Calibration information and the FastPCC code-access link are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to DeepRAHT and Slide Deformable Transformer, removes the PointNet and PointNet++ references, and drops the GRASP-Net discussion while retaining its citation in the introduction. The broader positioning around HRCS and cross-platform consistency remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar and terminology edits, corrects the Section 4.2 reference from Fig. 5 to Fig. 2(a), removes several supplementary-material pointers, and adds contribution footnotes and acknowledgements. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Fig. 2(a)'s subcaption changes from BD-rate to BD-PSNR, matching its unchanged axis. Existing architecture and ablation figures and result tables move between pages, and supplementary pagination restarts. The graphics and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the Fig. 2(a) metric label and the Section 4.2 figure reference resolves concrete sources of confusion, with additional modest gains from language and notation fixes. Removing the GRASP-Net explanation loses some context, but the methods, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain intact. The net improvement is limited to clarity and presentation.
